name: Valuation and Mispricing

concepts.concept: Market price vs. intrinsic value (mispricing is a basis, not proof)
concepts.summary: Price is observed; intrinsic value is a model estimate. Gaps signal opportunity, analysts can disagree, prices can embed scenario probabilities.

sources.note: differing views of value make a market; margin of safety

concepts.concept: Book value and price-to-book (limits in distress/liquidation)
concepts.summary: Book value = assets − liabilities; P/B = price/BVPS; intangibles justify premiums; forced sales can recover below book.

sources.note: conservative accounting deflates book; in recession/bankruptcy book may overstate true value; P/B formula

sources.section: Integrating Asset-Based and Cash Flow–Based Valuations
sources.note: book value as 'lower bound' that may need 30–50% haircut in distress sale

concepts.concept: Time value of money: PV, FV, discount rate, compounding
concepts.summary: PV = FV/(1+r)^n; discount rate = opportunity cost; later cash flows worth less; compound beats simple growth.

sources.section: Intrinsic Value: Dividend-Based Valuation — Time Value of Money
sources.note: PV = FV/(1+DR)^I; $10,000 note at 10% = $9,090.91; two-note PV sum

concepts.concept: Dividend discount model, perpetuity and terminal value
concepts.summary: Value = PV of dividends; perpetuity = D/r; higher r lowers value; distant cash flows carry much value.

sources.section: Intrinsic Value: Dividend-Based Valuation — The Dividend Discount Model
sources.note: Divco $1 dividend at 8%: 10-yr PV $6.71
perpetuity PV = D/DR = $12.50; years 11–∞ worth $5.79 (terminal-value intuition)

sources.note: cited by question pool; not in books/, unverified; WHFRD gives only the no-growth perpetuity D/DR — the Gordon D1/(r−g) formula and g<r condition are not in books/

concepts.concept: Growth-based valuation and growth sensitivity (growth vs. value labels)
concepts.summary: Projected growth compounds; small growth-assumption changes swing value nonlinearly; 'growth'/'value' are descriptors, not return guarantees.

sources.note: 'Small differences in growth assumptions can lead to big disparities in valuations' (p.34)
mature low-growth or troubled firms can trade near/below book (value-style context for G5Q3)

sources.book: Investopedia 'Growth Stock', 'Value Stock', 'Value Trap', 'Sustainable Growth Rate'; CFA style classification
sources.note: cited by question pool; not in books/, unverified; value-trap concept not named in WHFRD

concepts.concept: Scenario analysis, valuation ranges and margin of safety
concepts.summary: Probability-weight bear/base/bull cases; report a range, not false precision; margin of safety cushions but cannot eliminate error.

sources.note: base/pessimistic/optimistic scenarios; 'better to be roughly right than precisely wrong'; Graham margin of safety; buy below ~80 cents on the dollar
Graham: buy well below estimate of true value

concepts.concept: Trading mispricing: long/short, short-sale risk, timing and forced liquidation
concepts.summary: Long undervalued, short overvalued; shorts have unbounded loss and carry costs; correct thesis can still lose before convergence.

sources.note: short loss theoretically unlimited; short pays rebate/interest and dividends
